meta.title: Makeup placement rule base (brows, eyeliner, blush)
meta.scope: Placement and shape only. No colors, products, finishes or brands.
meta.approach: Balance and enhance natural features; rules are anchored to face landmarks.
meta.numeric_policy: Every number is an ESTIMATE unless a field explicitly says 'sourced'. No source gave degrees or percentages; all were qualitative.

labels.ESTIMATE: Proposed value, needs calibration and MUA validation
labels.INFERENCE: Analyst conclusion, not stated by sources
labels.CONFLICT: Sources disagree; options listed, one recommended

caveats: About 19 searches/page reads; many pages read only via snippets. Not exhaustive.
Most cells have 2-5 sources, not 3 fully independent ones. Independence is not verifiable; many Indonesian articles are translations of L'Oreal/Byrdie content.
Western and Indonesian tata rias rules are contrast-based/corrective (oval treated as ideal). The app's 'enhance, not correct' is a product framing, not a source principle.
meta.celebrity_note: Celebrity data is for reference/UI only and is NOT ground truth.

brow_start.rule: Vertical line from outer nose wing up to the brow

brow_tail.rule: Line from nose wing through outer eye corner; tail ends where it meets the brow

tail_level.rule: Tail should not end below the level of the brow start

recommended.label: ESTIMATE
recommended.reasoning: INFERENCE: with start at nose wing and tail at outer eye corner, outer iris edge falls near 70% of that span, so 'outer iris' and 'two-thirds' roughly coincide; pupil option (~50%) is the outlier.

blush_inner_limit.recommended: Hard inner limit at pupil vertical (most conservative); color starts at outer-iris vertical

blush_apex.rule: Start at highest cheekbone point under the outer eye corner, blend up toward hairline and in toward pupil

measurement_conditions.reason: Smiling lifts apples so blush sits lower on neutral face (S26); liner/crease visibility changes with eyes closed (S47, S48)

eye_shape.wing_angle_reference: Degrees from the extension of the lower lash line. Anchor sourced: wing aims toward the end of the brow (S40, S42). All degree/length values are ESTIMATE.

almond.definition: Symmetric, slightly tapered outer corner; neutral tilt (qualitative, S54)
almond.start: Inner corner, following natural lash line

round.definition: High height/width ratio; white visible above/below iris at neutral (S45); large lid space (S52)
special_notes: Goal is a more almond/oval impression (S46, S59)
conflicts: Dramatic upward wing (S42) vs not too upward (S44) vs liner pulled down the outer edge to elongate (S58)

hooded.definition: Crease close to lash line; fold overhangs outer lid; little lid space when eyes are open (S43, S45, S52). Crease is not a MediaPipe landmark.

wing.description: Flick up, joined to half of lower lash line (S44); square wing possible (S59)

hooded.lower_lash_line: deeper on outer third, angled upward (S45)
special_notes: Set liner with powder to reduce transfer (S42)

monolid.definition: Little or no visible crease; flat lid; liner disappears when eyes open (S45, S54). Measure visible lid height with eyes open. Crease not detectable via MediaPipe; likely needs image classifier or user confirmation.
monolid.start: Close to lash line, from inner corner or slightly in (S54, S55)
special_notes: Apply with eyes open (S47, S48, S51)
conflicts: Thicker line across the eye so it does not vanish: S40, S41, S48, S49, S54, S55
Line only the ends / wing: S50, S56
Avoid thick straight line across the whole eye: S53
monolid.gap: No named Indonesian MUA found; Indonesian sources are editorial/commercial. Priority for MUA validation.

upturned.definition: Outer corner higher than inner (S43, S45); tilt threshold ESTIMATE only

downturned.start: Keep inner corner open and bright; thin start (S41)

wing.description: Follow extension of lower lash line toward end of brow, subtle (S40); approx 0 deg offset

special_notes: Goal is lift at the outer corner (S41, S57)

close_set.definition: Gap between inner corners less than one eye width (S43, S44)
close_set.start: Inner corner, super thin to the middle (S42)

wing.description: Tapered, ends in line with brow tail (S42), near horizontal (S55)

wide_set.definition: Gap between inner corners more than one eye width (S45, S55)

wing.description: Do not extend past outer corner (S41); none or very short

blend_rules.status: INFERENCE (NO CONSENSUS FOUND in sources; only S65 mentions blended faces)
steps: Compute a continuous similarity score per face shape from landmark ratios; scores sum to 1.
If top score >= 0.6 and gap to second >= 0.2 (ESTIMATE), use the primary shape rules only.
Else continuous params (arch height level, blush angle, blush height) = score-weighted mean of the top two.
Categorical params (e.g. horizontal vs lifted blush) follow the primary shape.
For opposing pairs (e.g. round high arch vs heart low arch), choose the smallest change from the user's natural brow.

rules.rule: Local zone wins: eye shape (Table 2) controls the eye; face shape controls brow arch and blush only.
rules.reason: No source ties liner to face shape.

rules.rule: Shared lift vector: brow tail, wing and blush sweep point the same way or stay neutral.
One emphasis: thick wing (monolid, hooded) pairs with medium brows; avoid bold brow plus bold wing.
Wide-set eyes: no wing even if face shape suggests lift; lift comes from arch/blush.
Oblong face + downturned eyes: wing follows lower-lash extension, blush stays horizontal.
Round face + upturned eyes: keep high arch, wing horizontal.
Low confidence or conflicting rules: choose the neutral option (soft arch, blush at apex about 15 deg, wing along lash extension).
Measure on neutral expression with eyes open.

engineering_gaps: Crease/fold is not a MediaPipe landmark: hooded vs monolid needs a classifier or user confirmation.
Hairline is not a landmark: face length and forehead width are unreliable for face-shape ratios.
All ratio thresholds in sources are qualitative; thresholds must be calibrated on real data.
Arch height is ordinal only (flat/soft/medium/high); numeric mapping needs calibration.
